Memorandum

To:  Mindy Wilcox, AICP

From:  Sean Matsler

Date:  May 5, 2021

File No:  085689

Re:  Raising Cane’s - Special Use Permit No. 2021-005 (SP-2021-005)

Cox, Castle & Nicholson LLP represents Raising Cane’s Chicken Fingers in connection with
proposed Special Use Permit No. 2021-005 (SP-2021-005) at 401 South Prairie Avenue. Attached
as Appendix A are Raising Cane’s suggested revisions to the City’s draft conditions of approval,
which were sent to your attention by Bob Superneau of PM Design on May 4, 2021. Below is the
applicant’s written explanation to support and explain those suggested revisions.

On behalf of the entire Raising Cane’s team, we would like to thank City staff for their
professionalism and dedication throughout the entitlement process.

    Condition No. 3 – The applicant proposes new Condition No. 3 to memorialize the
  statement in the Staff Report that the operating hours for walk-in and drive-thru service
  will be from 9:00 AM to 3:30 AM, seven days a week.

    Condition No. 5 – The applicant proposes to eliminate the obligation to include an ordering
  kiosk inside the restaurant. We understand that such kiosks may be used by certain fast
  food restaurants, but they are not part of the applicant’s business and are not in use in any
  of its >500 restaurants.

    Condition No. 9 – The applicant proposes to revise Condition No. 9 to allow the City and
  applicant to work together to create a comprehensive ingress/egress traffic circulation and
  queuing management plan. This plan would include clear guidelines on when the applicant
  would be required to modify operations to accommodate additional on-site queuing, deploy
  temporary traffic monitors, and when the City could step-in to enforce those
  guidelines. The applicant shares the City’s goal to prevent vehicle queues from spilling on
  to surrounding public Right-of-Ways.

    Condition No. 10 – The applicant proposes to delete Condition No. 10, which would now
  be addressed by the comprehensive ingress/egress traffic circulation and queuing
  management plan as set forth in revised Condition No. 9.

    Condition No. 11 – The applicant proposes to revise Condition No. 11 and commits to
  working cooperatively on future sidewalk and turn lane dedications. As proposed,
  Condition No. 11 does not provide adequate detail regarding the dimensions of any
  dedications or their timing. The applicant is not opposed to such dedications but wants to
  better understand their scope before agreeing to an open-ended commitment.

    Condition No. 16 – The applicant proposes to clarify Condition No. 16 such that the traffic
  management plan would be reviewed and approved by the Traffic Division of the Public
  Works Department during Site Plan Review.

    Condition No. 19 – The applicant proposes to revise Condition No. 19 such that the term
  of the Special Use Permit could be extended by the Planning Commission, and to define
  the term “utilize” (in the context of the Condition) to mean that the applicant has applied
  for Site Plan Review.
